Subject: EU Egress: verification & action required to complete traffic reroute

Hi Patrick / Acme Ops team,

Quick update and an ask after the incident this morning: our infrastructure team completed the control-plane remediation in eu-west-1 at 08:40 UTC and started the automated reroute for impacted tenants at ~08:45. For most tenants the switch was automatic, but our analytics flagged that Acme Retail is still sending a small fraction (~4%) of calls to the old egress path.

We need one operational validation from your side to confirm the reroute is fully in effect from your edge: can your network team run the attached validation script (egress_reroute_instructions_v1.pdf) and reply with the small packet-capture screenshot outlined in step 3? That will let us close the incident for your account and issue a formal postmortem.

Key notes:
- Time window: please run validation any time in the next 24 hours.
- Traces to collect: sample request IDs listed on page 2 of the attachment.
- If you see >1% traffic still hitting the legacy egress, reply immediately; we will open a temporary backfill to reprocess those requests.

I'll loop in Lauren (network ops) and Grace (customer success) for any lift.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: EU Egress: verification & action required to complete traffic reroute

Ben / Patrick —

Following up with the technical details Patrick will need. A few clarifications for the validation:

Steps (condensed):
1) Run curl against the sample request IDs in the PDF; include header X-RW-Trace.
2) Capture the egress ASN and destination IP in the TCP handshake. Expected egress ASN: 39513 (Redwood-EU-primary).
3) If you still see legacy egress ASN 12345, stop the test and reply with the pcap.

If you prefer we can run a passive check from our side if you share a single ephemeral read-only S3 URL containing a 30s pcap (the script shows how). Grace: FYI, if Acme confirms >1% residual traffic we'll coordinate a limited replay window and a credit for the impacted token volume.

—Lauren
Network Reliability Lead
Redwood Inference
From: Patrick Lopez <patrick.lopez@acmeretail.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ops@acmeretail.com, grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 13 Jun 2028 08:17:00 +0100
Subject: Re: EU Egress: verification & action required to complete traffic reroute

Thanks Ben / Lauren —

We ran the quick validation per the PDF and attached the screenshot from tcpdump showing the destination IP (18.204.12.9) and ASN 39513. That matches what you listed. Sample trace IDs tested: rw-20280612-ACME-001, rw-20280612-ACME-002.

Result: 0.3% of requests were still observed hitting the legacy egress during the first 10m after the switch; after a second routing refresh at 09:05 UTC we observed 0.0%. Attaching verification screenshot.

Next steps from our side:
- We'll keep monitoring for 24h and forward any residual pcap if it reappears.
- If your team needs the pcap now for passive validation, tell us the S3 upload URL and we'll drop it there.

Patrick Lopez
NetOps Manager | Acme Retail

Patrick — thanks for the quick validation and the screenshot. Two small follow-ups:

1) Confirmation record: please reply to this thread with the line you prefer for the postmortem (one sentence) that we can attribute to Acme Ops, e.g. “Acme confirmed full reroute and no customer-facing impact after 09:05 UTC.” We include a one-line customer confirmation in our public postmortem.

2) Documentation & credits: Grace will follow up on the credit for the brief reprocessed volume and a short billing reconciliation; Karthik will coordinate the replay window should you want us to reprocess the <1% still-shifted requests (we have the buffer queued).

I'll schedule the postmortem for tomorrow and share the draft. For transparency I'm including the Drive link with the incident checklist: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2c-ops-checklist and our HubSpot record HS-12345 so your CS team can match notes.

If anything regresses, mark the thread urgent and we'll reopen the incident immediately.

Best,
